title: Expected discrete derivative under biased signs
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p=(p_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ satisfy $0<p_i<1$ for every coordinate, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and choose a coordinate $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. Under the independent product distribution whose coordinate signs have the biases specified by $p$, the expectation of the discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ equals the cube partial derivative of $f$ at the singleton $\{i\}$, evaluated with coordinate means $1-2p_j$: $\mathbb{E}[D_i f]=\partial_{\{i\}}f\bigl((1-2p_j)_j\bigr)$.
hypotheses_covered: Each parameter $p_i$ lies strictly between $0$ and $1$
